Radio

Radio
at
Pluto: F5OEO's DATV firmware (PlutoDVB2 is set over its MQTT). LibreSDR: DL1JM's DATV firmware. OpenHamShack sets its frequency, mode, symbol rate, FEC and power on the radio's own page before each transmission, keys it with PTT and checks it went on air, and always sends PTT off at the end. A LibreSDR that does not answer as that firmware is not keyed. Its on-air or standby state is in Diagnostics.

Screens

With a TV
One screen
Split: the picture in a column beside the console; nothing covers anything. Picture: the picture fills the screen, over a bar with Split, Console and TRANSMIT that hides after a while (a tap on the picture brings it back). Console: no picture.
This browser
Touch: large controls, for a touchscreen at arm's length. Compact: smaller, for a mouse and keyboard, with more on the page. Auto: Compact for a mouse and keyboard elsewhere, Touch on the box's own screen. Aa in the header switches too.

Transmission (advanced)

Roll-off
How steeply the signal's edges fall away. A smaller roll-off fits the same symbol rate into less bandwidth; receivers find any of the three. Leave it as it is unless the station you work asks otherwise.

Time-out
After this long on air the transmitter switches off by itself. A minute before, a bar at the top counts down with Keep transmitting, which starts the time again.
Busy check without BATC
When BATC's QO-100 spectrum cannot be reached, look at the band through the Pluto's own receiver rather than only offering Transmit anyway. Needs the LNB fed to the Pluto's RX port as well (a splitter with a DC block) and PlutoDVB2 with its spectrum; it changes the Pluto's receive settings, never while on air. Not yet tried on real hardware.

On the Pluto
The MiniTiouner or PicoTuner goes on a powered USB hub on the Pluto's USB port, and the Pluto on Ethernet (a USB Ethernet adapter in the same hub) at the radio's address: with the hub there, its USB link to this box is gone. The Pluto (PlutoDVB2) runs longmynd and sends the picture here. It starts with 18 V on the LNB until this box sets the LNB supply a second later: check what is on the F connector first. Not yet tried on real hardware.

Automatic reports
Send a report automatically when something goes wrong.
The same report as Send to the developer - the PC's make and model, its hardware and drivers, your callsign and settings with every password, PIN and key removed, and the logs - headed with what went wrong. It is sent when an update fails, the transmitter's video encoder stops with an error, the receiver keeps restarting, or OpenHamShack was not shut down properly (including the power being switched off at the wall). At most one of each kind every 6 hours and five a day, never while transmitting - it waits until you stop.
Daily check-in
Tell the developer once a day which version and PC this is - no callsign, location or logs.
A random number this box made up for itself, the OpenHamShack version and update channel, the PC's make, model and processor, whether its video encoder works, which kind of tuner is plugged in, and whether the radio is a Pluto or a LibreSDR. Nothing else - no callsign, locator, network addresses, settings or logs. It tells the developer which versions are in use and which PCs OpenHamShack is known to work on.

Back up

Your settings, the log and the overlay's pictures, in one file. Not recordings or videos: copy those with a PC. Screens, the update address and Wi-Fi stay with this PC.

DC on the coax. 13 V or 18 V powers the LNB up the receive cable, only while receiving through it. Leave it Off with a terrestrial antenna, a bias-T or a preamp not built for it: they can be damaged. 18 V picks QO-100's wideband (horizontal) on most LNBs. USB tuners with an LNB regulator only.

Updates

You are trying OpenHamShack from the USB stick, so OpenHamShack and operating-system updates are off: an update would be kept in memory only and lost at shutdown, and the stick starts the version it was made with every time. Install OpenHamShack to keep it up to date. Pluto and PicoTuner firmware can still be updated - that changes the radio and the tuner, not this PC.

Set up OpenHamShack

Getting the latest version

Before the questions, OpenHamShack makes sure it is the newest version, so that you set up on it.

Your callsign

Welcome. A few questions and a quick check of this PC, and OpenHamShack is ready to use.

Callsign
Sent with every transmission, in the picture and in the stream's name. OpenHamShack will not transmit until it is set.

Where you are

Locator
Your Maidenhead locator, 4 or 6 characters (IO85 or IO85jw). Optional: it is used for ISS passes, the weather on the picture overlay and the log.

Your radio

Radio
Address
A Pluto plugged in by USB is usually at 192.168.2.1. A LibreSDR is on your network: its address is in your router's list of devices. The radio must run DATV firmware (F5OEO's for a Pluto, DL1JM's for a LibreSDR); OpenHamShack sets the radio's frequency and power itself.

Your receiver

Tuner
PicoTuner
USB tuner: a MiniTiouner, or a PicoTuner with its USB firmware - found by itself. PicoTuner network: a PicoTuner with the Ethernet firmware, at the address it shows. Tuner on the Pluto: the tuner on a powered USB hub on the Pluto, with the Pluto on Ethernet; the Pluto's own longmynd runs it (PlutoDVB2, not yet tried on real hardware). None: transmit only.

Your licence

Region
OpenHamShack will not transmit outside the amateur bands your choice allows. Scotland also covers within 40 km of the Scottish border or coast. IARU Region 1 is Europe, Africa and the Middle East.

Checking this PC

Up to half a minute. Nothing is transmitted.
